title: 1 Samuel 3:19–21
context: Samuel grows up, the LORD is with him, and none of his words fall to the ground, so all Israel from Dan to Beersheba recognizes him as a prophet of the LORD. The LORD continues to appear at Shiloh, revealing himself to Samuel by his word. Both traditions read this as shared ground on God’s faithfulness in restoring his word to Israel through a trustworthy prophet.

verses.text: Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
verses.arminianNotes:
Samuel grows, the LORD is with him, and none of his words fall to the ground. Arminian readers note that Samuel’s faithfulness and God’s presence go together.

His words prove true, a mark of a genuine prophet (Deut 18:21–22).
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see God’s presence as the source of Samuel’s authority.

It is the LORD who lets none of his words fall, so the reliability of the prophet rests on God.

verses.text: All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of the LORD.
verses.arminianNotes:
All Israel from Dan to Beersheba knows Samuel is established as a prophet. Arminian readers note the nationwide recognition (cf. Judg 20:1 for the phrase).

The people’s response confirms God’s work.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see God establishing his prophet before the whole nation.

The phrase “from Dan even to Beersheba” means the whole land, north to south.

verses.text: The LORD appeared again in Shiloh; for the LORD revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by the LORD’s word.
verses.arminianNotes:
The LORD appeared again in Shiloh, revealing himself to Samuel by his word. Arminian readers note the reversal of verse 1: the word that was rare is now given.

In the engwebp edition this verse ends the chapter, and the next sentence, “The word of Samuel came to all Israel,” opens 4:1.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers see God’s self-revelation through his word as central. God reveals himself “by the LORD’s word.”

The renewal of revelation at Shiloh comes just before the disaster of chapter 4.
